senses.gloss:
Rantideva
------------------------------------------
Sacrificing oneself for the good of others has always been considered as a great virtue in हिन्दुइस्म्. One of the greatest examples found in the epics and the पुराणस् is that of the king रन्तिदेव. He was the son of Saṅkṛti and belonged to the चन्द्रवṁश (the lunar race). He had performed many yāgas or वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्.
He was once doing severe austerities in a forest along with his family. As a part of this, he fasted for 48 days. On the 49th day he received divine ड़ोओद्, just enough for him and his family.
As the family was getting ready to partake of the ड़ोओद्, a few hungry guests came one after another. रन्तिदेव gave away all the ड़ोओद्, including the meagre drinking water.
These guests who were actually the Trimūrtis (Brahmā, विष्णु and शिव) appeared before him. रन्तिदेव honoured them with devoted obeisance but never asked for any boon! The gods then granted him and his family highest spiritual wisdom (vide Bhāgavata 9.21).
According to the Mahābhārata (Droṇaparva 67), the king रन्तिदेव was very fond of feeding guests sumptuously and offering them gifts liberally.
See also CARMAṆVATĪ.
